$comment: World fields (ruleset v0): integer grids on the map's field cells (tech notes, section 6; spec S1, docs/design/spec-s1-water.md). Water depth is in micrometres (S1: rain and runoff add fractions of a millimetre per step), and each cell keeps four outflows in um/s of its own depth (virtual pipes, S1 section 2). Wetness and mud are on 0-65535. nav_speed holds navigation's per-class speed codes (M3 item 5). tileCells: cells per side of an activity tile (16 = 24 m); sleepAfterSteps: quiet field steps before a tile sleeps (S1: 5). The water numbers are S1 proposals, tuned against the M3 tests, so the file is marked placeholder.

fields.$comment: Navigation's speed codes, one byte per class (foot, horse, wheeled): 0 swept, 1 too deep, else speed permille / 4. Written by navigation once per refresh from water and mud, never by a field model; 16448250 is full speed for all three.

ground.$comment: S1 sections 5 and 6. Wetness: 2 units per um soaked in (full, 65535, is about 32.8 mm); standing water (at least the dry depth) soaks in at 1 mm/s; ground with no standing water dries at 110 a second, down to the field's initial wetness (the map's natural moisture; S1 says to dry, this stops it at the natural level so a dry map stays asleep). Mud: untrodden ground above 32768 wetness is mud of (wetness - 32768) by itself; the most mud a wetness allows is (wetness - 16384) x 4 / 3, times the soil's cap; each moving unit adds churnWeight[class] x 96 x soil churn x (wetness - 16384) / 49151 per field step. Churn weights are roughly mass ratios until S2.

soils.$comment: A firm road: gets soft, never deep.

water.$comment: S1 section 2. pipeGainPermille = g * dt / cell = 9.81 * 0.1 / 1.5. Bed friction (S1's damping stand-in, made depth-aware) is the shallow-water coefficient c_f in millionths, tuned so the M3 river runs about 0.5 to 1 m/s at base flow: 0.0042, a normal river bed. The deadbands (S1's 1 mm/s and 1 mm sleep thresholds) let still water go quiet: a flow under 1 mm/s with under 1 mm of head behind it stops.
